title: Session 14: .NET Core Development and the Future

questions.questionText: .NET Core is
options: a cross-platform, open-source framework from Microsoft
questions.correctAnswer: a cross-platform, open-source framework from Microsoft
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C) a cross-platform, open-source framework from Microsoft. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which operating systems does .NET Core support?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) Windows, Linux, and macOS. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: .NET Core is best suited for
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) cross-platform and cloud-based/microservice applications. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which is a reason to use .NET Core?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C) Cross-platform needs and high performance. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: When should you NOT use .NET Core?
options: When your app depends on Windows-specific technologies not available in .NET Core
questions.correctAnswer: When your app depends on Windows-specific technologies not available in .NET Core
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A) When your app depends on Windows-specific technologies not available in .NET Core. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: .NET Framework is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) Windows-only. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Porting from .NET Framework to .NET Core often involves
options: using tools like the .NET Portability Analyzer
questions.correctAnswer: using tools like the .NET Portability Analyzer
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) using tools like the .NET Portability Analyzer. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which tool analyzes API compatibility when porting?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) .NET Portability Analyzer. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: .NET Core supports side-by-side installation of
options: multiple versions on the same machine
questions.correctAnswer: multiple versions on the same machine
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D) multiple versions on the same machine. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which CLI is used to create and run .NET Core apps?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) dotnet. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command creates a new console project?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C) dotnet new console. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command builds a .NET project?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D) dotnet build. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command runs a .NET project?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) dotnet run. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command restores NuGet packages?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C) dotnet restore. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command publishes an app for deployment?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) dotnet publish. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command runs unit tests?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A) dotnet test. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: .NET Core projects use a project file with extension
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D) .csproj. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: The project's package manager in .NET is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A) NuGet. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: The runtime for .NET Core apps is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D) CoreCLR. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: The JIT compiler in .NET Core is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C) RyuJIT. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: ASP.NET Core is
options: a cross-platform framework for web apps and APIs
questions.correctAnswer: a cross-platform framework for web apps and APIs
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D) a cross-platform framework for web apps and APIs. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: .NET Core 3.1 is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D) a long-term support (LTS) release. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: .NET 5.0 unifies
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D) .NET Core and .NET Framework features. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Starting with .NET 5, the name dropped
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) the word "Core". (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which .NET release follows .NET 5.0 in the unified platform plan?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) .NET 6. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: The "future" of .NET is described as a single unified platform for
options: desktop, web, cloud, mobile, gaming, IoT, and AI
questions.correctAnswer: desktop, web, cloud, mobile, gaming, IoT, and AI
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) desktop, web, cloud, mobile, gaming, IoT, and AI. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which tool produces a self-contained deployment?
options: dotnet publish with a runtime identifier
questions.correctAnswer: dotnet publish with a runtime identifier
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) dotnet publish with a runtime identifier. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: In a framework-dependent deployment, the target machine must have
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A) the .NET runtime installed. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: In a self-contained deployment, the app
options: requires the runtime to be installed
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D) includes the .NET runtime. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which target moniker is used for .NET Core 3.1?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A) netcoreapp3.1. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which target moniker is used for .NET Framework 4.8?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) net48. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command shows installed SDKs?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) dotnet --list-sdks. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command shows installed runtimes?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A) dotnet --list-runtimes. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which command displays the installed .NET version?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) dotnet --version. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: A benefit of open source for .NET Core is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) community contributions on GitHub. (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: In .NET Core, the Main entry point is
options: the same Main method (or top-level statements)
questions.correctAnswer: the same Main method (or top-level statements)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A) the same Main method (or top-level statements). (.NET Core Development and the Future)

questions.questionText: Which tool is the cross-platform editor from Microsoft that works with .NET Core?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) Visual Studio Code. (.NET Core Development and the Future)
